problem: The chapter defines k-colourable as using at most k colours (unused colours allowed), then says a k-colouring splits V into exactly k independent sets. If a colour is unused its class is empty, so the count can be less than k. A student may think all k colours must appear.
fix: A k-colouring splits V into at most k independent sets; some colour classes may be empty.

problem: 'A graph is bipartite exactly when it is 2-colourable exactly when it has no odd cycle' is correct, but the trap later repeats it as 'bipartite graphs are exactly the 2-colourable graphs with no odd cycle', which is redundant and reads as if 2-colourable graphs might have odd cycles.
fix: In the trap write: 'bipartite graphs are exactly the 2-colourable graphs, and these are exactly the graphs with no odd cycle.'

problem: The BFS argument 'a breadth-first search from any vertex assigns alternating colours' silently assumes a connected graph; a disconnected graph needs a BFS in each component.
fix: If there is no odd cycle, a breadth-first search from any vertex assigns alternating colours; repeat for each connected component.

problem: 'An empty graph is 3-colourable but has χ = 1' is ambiguous: many textbooks use 'empty graph' for the graph with no vertices, whose chromatic number is 0. As written the example can look wrong.
fix: 'A graph with no edges on four vertices is 3-colourable but has χ = 1.'

problem: Grammar: 'χ is the minimum registers needed' is missing a noun.
fix: χ is the minimum number of registers needed.

problem: The name is misspelt; the standard spelling carries an accent.
